primary_source.citation: Buck, W. R. (1991), Modes of continental lithospheric extension, Journal of Geophysical Research, 96(B12), 20161-20178, doi:10.1029/91JB01485.
primary_source.source_policy: Buck 1991 is the primary equation authority. The supplied clear PDF page images (SHA256 0f545e0c045db989bd81ae62461cebfd5e52d72eeb6ed1d9b8c326374e8d5d26) were visually inspected for the page/equation references recorded in the registry; image inspection, not OCR, controls mathematical transcription. Literal source inconsistencies are retained and labeled. No later model replaces Buck and no ARCANA parameters are selected.

equation_inventory.output: temperature T(z,t) at center of the extension zone
dependencies: volumetric heating divided by ρCp, H
equation_inventory.units: K s^-1 on both sides; κ m² s^-1; v m s^-1; H K s^-1
equation_inventory.support: one-dimensional vertical column at rift center; nonextending region temperature is held unchanged
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (1), p. 20163. The printed source symbol is H; the adjacent text defines it as crustal radiogenic heat production divided by density and specific heat (K s^-1), while Table 2 reports the underlying volumetric heat production (W m^-3). Lateral conduction is omitted.

equation_inventory.units: Pa; g B Pa m^-1; z m
equation_inventory.support: vertical crust/mantle lithosphere profile
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (2), p. 20164. B is Buck’s extensional brittle-failure constant (kg m^-3); gB is the stress gradient. Effective pore-pressure assumptions are incorporated in gB.

equation_inventory.output: ductile flow stress at imposed strain rate
equation_inventory.units: ε̇ s^-1; σ Pa; A Pa^-n s^-1; E J mol^-1; R J mol^-1 K^-1; T K
equation_inventory.support: each vertical material layer; crust and mantle use separately assigned rheology
equation_inventory.time: evaluated as T, strain rate and geometry change
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (3), p. 20164. T is absolute temperature. Inverted form is algebraically equivalent, not the literal displayed form.

equation_inventory.kind: derived algebraic profile plus depth integral
equation_inventory.support: vertical column at the extension-zone center; total force per unit horizontal length
equation_inventory.notes: The paper explicitly defines yield as the lesser brittle or ductile stress and integrated strength as its depth integral. Appendix A gives special analytic envelope formulae, not the general numerical calculation.

equation_inventory.support: vertical lower-crust half-space
equation_inventory.time: effective closure parameterized for a calculation
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (4), p. 20166. The exponent is positive y/y_0.

dependencies: boundary conditions at Moho and upper half-space
equation_inventory.support: vertical lower-crust profile at horizontal x
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (5), p. 20166. The negative sign and both y factors are visible; u_f(0)=u_f(∞)=0.

equation_inventory.output: horizontal pressure gradient driving lower-crust flow
equation_inventory.support: lateral model cross-section
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (6), p. 20166: Δρ*=ρ_c(ρ_m−ρ_c)/ρ_m. Table 1, p. 20164, prints the reversed order; this source-internal definition inconsistency is recorded and not silently reconciled.

equation_inventory.support: symmetric lateral interval x∈[0,X_L/2] representing half of a 2-D section
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (7), p. 20166. Buck states the last two terms describe advection and thinning by prescribed velocity; Eq. (7) is strictly valid for Newtonian viscosity.

equation_inventory.support: spatially uniform closure parameter over x, varying with time in Buck's model
equation_inventory.time: paper states κ_f varies in time but not space
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (8), p. 20166; κ_f varies in time but not space in this model.

equation_inventory.output: Newtonian-equivalent viscosity parameters for the non-Newtonian crust flow closure
equation_inventory.units: η_0 Pa s; y_0 m; κ_f m² s^-1
equation_inventory.support: base of crust and flow profile
equation_inventory.time: closure evaluated from the thermal/rheologic state
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (9), p. 20166. The adjacent text defines C = A⁻¹(2 y_0 ∂P/∂x)^(1−n); the stress 2 y_0 ∂P/∂x is the average deviatoric stress at the crust base, with 1 MPa minimum in model calculations.

equation_inventory.output: effective lower-crust viscosity/scale or diffusivity inputs used by Eq. 8
equation_inventory.units: closure-dependent; η_0 Pa s, y_0 m, κ_f m² s^-1
equation_inventory.support: lower crust at extension support
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (10), p. 20167. The adjacent text states that ∂T/∂z is the thermal gradient at the Moho; the formula itself has no printed M subscript on that derivative.

equation_inventory.form: ε̇=U_x/X_e; velocity varies linearly across the prescribed pure-shear extension zone
equation_inventory.kind: kinematic forcing definition (not a numbered equation in this registry)
equation_inventory.output: finite extension forcing and local thinning
equation_inventory.units: U_x m s^-1; X_e m; ε̇ s^-1; strain dimensionless
equation_inventory.support: central zone |x|≤X_e/2; symmetric section
equation_inventory.notes: Table 1 and Figure 2 define ε̇=U_x/X_e and linear velocity change over X_e. B is the separate brittle-failure constant in Table 1/Eq. 2. Extension is imposed, not predicted from plate motion.

equation_inventory.output: buoyancy force from isostatically compensated density anomaly
equation_inventory.units: N m^-1 for force per section length under Buck's normalization
equation_inventory.support: thin-sheet, laterally long-wavelength anomalies relative to vertical extent
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (11), p. 20167. No additional horizontal length factor L appears. It is the vertical moment of isostatically compensated density anomaly per section length.

dependencies: thickness difference δh between x=0 and x=X_L/2
equation_inventory.support: small crustal-thickness perturbations
equation_inventory.time: force component at an evaluated state
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified directly from Eq. (12), p. 20167, for small crustal-thickness perturbations; δh is the center-to-edge thickness contrast.

equation_inventory.form: ARCANA_ADAPTATION: ΔF_i = F_i(final)−F_i(initial); ΔF_total = ΔF_ys + ΔF_tb + ΔF_cb
equation_inventory.output: signed change in local force required for continued extension
equation_inventory.support: local extension-zone column plus crust-thickness contrast to outer model edge
equation_inventory.time: after a prescribed finite extension amount
equation_inventory.notes: SOURCE_INTERNAL_SIGN_INCONSISTENCY: p. 20165 prose prints dF_ys=F_ys(initial)−F_ys(final), while Fig. 4 p. 20165 says positive dF_ys means strengthening, and A2/A8 pp. 20174–20175 make rapid-extension weakening negative. The internally consistent normalized convention is final−initial for each component (ARCANA_ADAPTATION), preserving the literal prose conflict. Under Appendix extension convention dF_cb>0, dF_tb<0 in the rapid thermal-buoyancy expression, and total force change is their signed sum with dF_ys. Buck p. 20168 states positive total dF means force required for continued local extension increases; Buck assumes widening. Negative dF favors localized extension. Diagnostic only; not an ARCANA topology transition.

equation_inventory.support: vertical brittle-envelope approximation
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified from A1–A2, p. 20174. In A1, if Z_m<h, the term (Z_m²−h²) is set to zero. A2 is a rapid-extension approximation with negligible thermal diffusion.

equation_inventory.form: A3: δρ = 2α ρ_m(T_m−T_s)(1−z/(2Z_m)); A4: dF_tb = −[1−exp(−2ε)] gα ρ_m(T_m−T_s)Z_m²/6
equation_inventory.support: Appendix assumed thermal profile and brittle-mantle thickness
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified from A3–A4, p. 20174. A3 is the linear thermal-density profile; A4 is the rapid-extension thermal buoyancy change.

equation_inventory.support: infinite-width approximation; appendix permits flow to infinity unlike finite numerical no-flow boundaries
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified from A5, p. 20174, and A6–A7, p. 20175. A5 permits flow to ±∞, unlike the finite no-flow numerical boundaries. Appendix formal validity requires the initial thickness change δh to be of order y_0 or less.

equation_inventory.form: A8: G_z=dF_cb/(−dF_ys); A9: G_z=[Δρ*h²/{B(Z_c²+Z_m²−h²)}]F(κ_f,ε̇); A10: F=1 if √(κ_f ε/ε̇)≪X_e, and F=X_e/[2√(κ_f ε/ε̇)] if √(κ_f ε/ε̇)≫X_e
equation_inventory.support: limiting assumptions above
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified from A8–A10, p. 20175. This is the Appendix analytical approximation only: neglect thermal-buoyancy force change, rapid extension for A8, small-strain limit for A9, and asymptotic length-scale limits for A10. Never substitute G_z for the full numerical model.

equation_inventory.form: A11: T_c = E/{nR ln[g B h(A/ε̇)^(1/n)]}; A12: κ_f=(gΔρ*/C)[hRT_M²/{E(T_M−T_s)}]³ exp[−E/(RT_M)]
equation_inventory.support: linear geotherm / specified rheology approximation
equation_inventory.notes: Page-image verified from A11, p. 20175, and A12, p. 20176. A11 solves the brittle/ductile transition under the stated approximation; A12 assumes a linear geotherm. Both remain Appendix approximations, not substitutes for the full numerical solution.

additional_sign_evidence: p. 20163 Eq. 1; p. 20164 Eq. 2–3; p. 20165 Table 3/Fig. 4 and prose defining dF_ys
p. 20167 Eq. 11–12 and text identifying thermal buoyancy

literal_source_statements.statement: positive dF_ys means the lithosphere gets stronger on extension
rapid-extension dF_ys = −[1−exp(−2ε)] times the initial positive strength expression; weakening is negative
G_z = dF_cb/(−dF_ys); rapid-extension dF_ys is negative

force_sign_audit.internally_consistent_convention: ARCANA_ADAPTATION: interpret signed component changes as final minus initial, so strength weakening is negative; retain the conflicting p. 20165 prose literally as source inconsistency.

extension_signs.dF_cb: positive for extension in A6 and source prose
extension_signs.dF_tb: negative for rapid-extension thermal buoyancy in A4

interpretation.positive_total: required force for continued local extension increases; Buck assumes widening
interpretation.negative_total: localization is favored; narrow-rift or core-complex mode depends on lower-crust flow

force_sign_audit.scope: Buck model diagnostic only; not an ARCANA topology transition.

additional_source_inconsistency.treatment: Preserve both forms. Eq. 6 p. 20166 is the positive reduced contrast used by Eq. 8, A6/A9 and the positive-for-extension text; Table 1 is retained as printed. Do not silently rewrite Table 1.

equations_recovered_scope_limit: The requested equation glyphs are recovered. This does not supply ARCANA pre-T1 state, material/rheology authority, or B6N2-to-Buck section forcing.

source_internal_inconsistencies.description: The prose defines dF_ys as initial minus final, opposite the figure and Appendix weakening sign.
Table 1 prints Δρ*=ρ_c(ρ_c−ρ_m)/ρ_m, while Eq. 6 defines Δρ*=ρ_c(ρ_m−ρ_c)/ρ_m. A6/A9 positive-extension interpretation is consistent with the Eq. 6 sign; retain the Table 1 literal conflict.

dimensional_checks.check: (ε̇/A)^(1/n) is Pa and E/(nRT) is dimensionless.
y/y_0 is dimensionless; η has Pa s.
Exponential argument E/(RT_M) is dimensionless; η_0 and C have Pa s.
Both expressions have force-per-section-length units N m^-1; Eq. 11 needs no extra horizontal L.
gB times a squared length has N m^-1; ε is dimensionless.
A3 is kg m^-3; A4 has N m^-1.
Error-function arguments and exponential/asymptotic conditions are dimensionless; A5 has length units.
A6 has N m^-1; A8/A9 are dimensionless under Buck’s B and Δρ* definitions.
The logarithm argument gBh(A/ε̇)^(1/n) is dimensionless; result has temperature units.

model_scope_separation.relationship: Appendix A8–A12 are limited analytical approximations and do not substitute for the full numerical model.
